Lakeside map rework: three options

Written for Oscar. Three reworked layouts of the main lakeside map, judged over three rounds against the current one. Core pieces are all kept: fishing dock, Marlow's stall, the Smokehouse, the casino gate with its posters, the Top Anglers, Thanks and Furthest Out boards, plus Reed's harbour, the mirror, the campfire, the worm patch, the square, the six houses, the townsfolk and the seven bottles. Nothing in the game has been changed; these are plans.

1. Harbour crescent2. Boardwalk and hillside3. The pointCurrent mapHow they were judged

The judge's verdict

All three keep every core piece, stay inside today's size and performance budgets, and fix the same faults in today's map: the shop and smokehouse now flank the pier's foot so the everyday loop is 13-17 s instead of a 60 m march, the boards stand where the loop passes them, Reed's harbour has its own beach, the campfire has a view, and the shore has a shape. They differ in what the town is.

  • 1. Harbour crescent, hybrid (37/40). The strongest sense of place: a cove framed by two pine-topped headlands, a working quay with the stalls facing the water, a bench jetty looking across at the campfire headland. After Oscar asked which of the top two was best, it took Boardwalk's three playability ideas (2026-11-08): the Top Anglers and Thanks boards at the pier root, the square as a junction of a village ring, and a second jetty so there are two lakeward cast spots besides the T. Pick this. The boards and mirror stand on the quay deck, which the build has to allow for.
  • 2. Boardwalk and hillside (35/40). The tightest everyday loop, all on timber, with the stalls and all three boards a few steps along the planks and the square as the junction behind. Pick this for play feel and the least friction. It is the least dramatic shore of the three and the gate is the longest walk from the square (10 s).
  • 3. The point (34/40). The most distinctive map: water on three sides, a pier that crosses a short bridge to Lantern Rock over deep water, a quiet beginner cove with a jetty and lily pads, a harbour basin, and the well square at the pier's foot with every service on its rim. Pick this for a map that feels like a new place to explore. It needs one new simple mesh (the rock islet), and the narrow bridge could bunch a crowd.

Recommendation. Harbour crescent, in its hybrid form above. The remaining questions (the cove at a phone's field of view, whether the quay feels crowded, the headland pines at dusk) can only be answered by a terrain-and-docks greybox in the engine, which is the natural first build step.

Each option below shows the plan to scale, the author's summary, what changed in the last round, hero views to stage in-engine, and the measured walks. Every plan is also a JSON layout in the engine's own terms (shore radii, pad, dock rectangles, spots with facing), ready to be turned into a build.

1. Harbour crescent 37 / 40

Judge: recommended. Best place, now with Boardwalk's hub: a real cove, a harbour front on a quay, Top Anglers at the pier root, Furthest Out on Reed's beach, two jetties, a village ring, the campfire seen across the water. Loop 15 s. Boards and mirror stand on the deck.

Harbour crescent, round 5 (hybrid)

Summary for Oscar

The town wraps a small cove like a fishing harbour: two pine-topped headlands frame the water and the pier runs straight out between them from a timber quay. The first cast looks at open lake, mountains and a rock islet; turning round shows the whole village along the waterfront.

Where things went. Marlow's Bait & Tackle and the Smokehouse flank the pier's foot on the quay, facing the water, the Fishmonger and Net Mender beside them. Top Anglers and Thanks hang on the quay beside the Smokehouse, a few steps from the pier root, so the leaderboard is the first thing passed after a catch; the wardrobe mirror is at the quay's east end by the bench jetty. Captain Reed's corner is the quay's west end: a wide lane runs down past the worm patch to his beach, the Furthest Out board stands at the top of it beside his lamp, and the seaplane floats in the cove in view from the pier and both jetties. A second jetty west of the pier, the rowboat moored beside it, gives two lakeward casting spots off the main pier. The well square is the junction up the main path: lanes from it run west past Wren's Cottage down to the worm patch and the quay, and east past the Net Mender down to the campfire headland, so the village is a ring rather than a corridor; three more houses stagger up to the casino gate, which closes the path. Reed, his Charters sign and the dive landing spot have their own beach under the west headland, five seconds from the shop; the rowboat is moored by the west jetty. The campfire sits on the east headland, seen across the water from the jetty bench.

What is new. A cove with framing headlands, a working quay with crates and lanterns, two jetties, a far islet, a rest stop on the walk up, a village ring, and a loop that passes the boards at the pier root.

Cost. Same houses, lamps (22) and point lights (8) as today; one more dock rectangle (5); about 17 more small props (rocks, reeds, pines, a bench). No new kinds of mesh.

Risks. Boards and mirror stand on the quay deck; sideways casts inside the cove reach the headland beaches at about 15 m (the game shortens a cast until it lands in water), so long rods cast lakeward from the T end and the jetties; hill puddles from the noise terrain, as today.

What changed in round 5 (Reed's corner)

Oscar worried that Reed's charters sat off the main loop and asked for the Furthest Out board by the activity it ranks. The walks to Reed were already as today's (22 m from the T end and the shop; 34 m and 43 m in the other two plans), so the fix was to make the quay's west end his corner rather than to move him:

1. Furthest Out on Reed's beach at (−19.2,8.2), facing up the lane, under the lit lamp at (−19,5), with the worm patch (−18.6,12) beside it: the charter leaderboard stands where charters start, as it does today. Ground 0.61 m, dry.

2. Reed's lane widened from 1.6 m to 2.4 m from the quay's west end (−13,13.5) to the Charters sign, so it reads as a street of the town, not a track.

3. The mirror to the east end at (11.6,13.3) by the bench jetty, the crates to the deck corner (12.4,10.9). Shop to mirror is 17.6 m.

Reed stays on his own beach: pulling him up against the quay is what crammed every round-one harbour. A sightline from the quay to the board is on the plan.

What changed in round 4 (the hybrid, by the judge)

Three ideas folded in from Boardwalk and hillside, after Oscar asked which of the two was best:

1. Boards at the pier root. Top Anglers and Thanks moved from the quay's east end to (7.2,12.8) on the deck, facing the pier root, beside the Smokehouse and under the lamp at (9.8,13.8); the crates slid east to (10.3,12.4). Shop to leaderboard is now 13.5 m. Furthest Out stays at (12.4,10.9) by the bench jetty.

2. The square as a junction: a village ring. Two lanes (1.6 m) leave the square's existing side lanes: west from (−9,32.3) past Wren's Cottage and behind the Fishmonger to the worm patch and the quay's west path at (−15.5,11.2); east from (6,33.7) past the blue house and behind the Net Mender down to the campfire path at (15.5,8.5). Both run on dry ground (0.5-0.9 m) just outside the pad. An unlit lamp on each at z 20; the worm patch moved beside the lane to (−18.6,12); Wren's flower bed to (−11,35.5).

3. A second jetty. A mirror of the bench jetty at x −8.75..−6.25, z 4..10, with the rowboat moored in the water beside it at (−10.3,6.2) and the reeds moved to (−11.5,8). Both jetties cast lakeward (−z) into open water; today's side piers cast sideways, which the cove does not allow past about 15 m.

Checked and left alone: the quay's end ramps already existed as the paths to Reed's beach and the campfire, so nothing to add. The headland tips stand only 0.4-0.6 m above the water (the hills term starts at the shore), so the pines (6-8 m) make the silhouette; from spawn and the T end they sit 75-90° off the lake axis, outside the camera's view, so they never hide the mountains and frame the cove when the player turns.

What changed in round 3

1. A pocket on the axis between the stalls and the square: a bench at (−4.6,24.5) facing the path, a flower bed at (−6.6,22.6) in front of the Fishmonger, under the existing lamp at (−2.8,22). The walk up now has a stop at z 22-25.

2. A three-rock islet at (−9,−36.5), (−7.2,−38.2), (−10.8,−38), radii 1.5/1.0/0.8, 30 m past the T end and 9 m off the pier's centre line, in 8-9 m of water; added as a sightline from the T end. The frame was extended to z −46 to show it.

3. Build notes: the boards (11.8,13.4), (12.4,10.9) and the mirror (−11.5,13.3) stand on the quay deck at height 0.7, not on terrain. The quay's rear edge (z 14.5) meets the pad bank flush at the centre (ground 0.75 against the 0.7 deck, like the pier foot today); at the ends (x ±10) the deck stands about 0.2 m proud of the sand, a kerb, which the pier root's 0.2 m step already matches.

4. Everything else is as in round 2: pad (0,37) r 21.5, shore, docks, houses, spots, NPC walks, bottles, lights (8 point lights). Props 69 (round 2: 64); round 4: 71.

2. Boardwalk and hillside 35 / 40

Judge: best loop. Stalls and boards on the planks at the pier root, the square as the junction behind, lamps in a line along the water. Loop 13 s. Longest walk to the gate.

Boardwalk and hillside (round 3)

Summary for Oscar

Concept. The town turns to face the lake: a timber boardwalk runs along the waterfront and the pier grows out of its middle, so Marlow's, the Smokehouse and the boards are a few steps along the planks. Behind it the street climbs through the well square to the casino gate, where the hill begins.

Where things are. Spawn is mid-pier, looking at a rock islet, the T end 10 m ahead. Marlow's and the Smokehouse flank the pier root; Top Anglers, Thanks and Furthest Out stand behind the right wing. The well square, mirror on its rim, is the junction 15 m up: ramps from both wing ends, a lane west to the campfire pocket (looking back at the pier), a lane east to the Fishmonger and racks. Reed, the CHARTERS sign and the seaplane have their own beach in the east cove; worm patch, rowboat and lily pads are in the west cove under Net Mender's. Wren's Cottage and three houses stagger up the street, a bench stop halfway, to the gate.

New. A waterfront hub; the everyday loop (pier end, shop, smokehouse, back) is about 13 s on timber; two coves, a headland, an islet; the gate backed by a hill.

Cost vs today. Same 22 lamps (8 real lights) and 6 houses; one more dock rectangle; about 20 more small props; no new meshes or textures.

Risks. The boardwalk's land side rests on sand just under the deck; Furthest Out stands a step above the deck; Reed's beach sits under the east hill.

What changed in round 3

Marlow's moved 1 m west (stall at (5.5,11.3), Smokehouse mirrored) so there is 2 m clear between its awning and Top Anglers (11.3,11.4); Furthest Out came down to the wing at (14.3,10.9) (ground 1.05; the suggested (13.5,11.3) is a 1.4 m bump); the right ramp now starts 2 m behind the wing end at (16.5,12.5), off the row of boards. A three-rock islet at (8,−37) sits 28 m beyond the T end, right of the pier line, with a sightline from the T. A street stop halfway to the gate: bench (−4.3,41.8) facing the street, lit lamp (−2.6,43), flower bed (−6.8,41.3) at the purple house's lane; the fences shortened so the lanes no longer cross them. Pip now laps the well inside the square and leaves by the east lane's north edge to the rack by the Fishmonger, off both ramps and the street exits. The left-wing bench moved to (−11,11.3) off the left ramp. Everything else as in round 2.

3. The point 34 / 40

Judge: most distinctive. Water on three sides, Lantern Rock over deep water, a beginner cove, a harbour basin, every service on the square at the pier's foot. Loop 17 s. One new simple mesh.

The point, round 3

Summary for Oscar

The town sits on a round point with water on three sides, and each side fishes differently: the pier runs off the tip over a short railed bridge to Lantern Rock, a lantern-lit rock islet over deep water where the big ones bite; the west side is a quiet cove with a short jetty, lily pads, reeds, the campfire and the worm patch for beginners; the south-east is Captain Reed's harbour, a sheltered basin where the seaplane moors nose to the sand. The well square sits at the foot of the pier so every walk crosses it, and the casino gate closes the road at the far end with hills behind.

Marlow's and the Smokehouse face the well from the square's lake side; Top Anglers, Thanks and Furthest Out stand together on its back rim, the wardrobe mirror opposite. Reed, his CHARTERS sign and the landing spot have their own beach 19 m from the shop. Six houses face the lake behind the square; halfway up the road a lit lamp, bench and flower bed make a stop.

New: the point with two bays, the islet, the beginner jetty, the basin, services on the square, a ~17 s loop.

Cost: 6 houses, 18 lamp posts with 8 point lights (today 22/8), 4 timber rectangles, ~65 props, one new simple mesh (the islet).

Risks: a steep headland behind the harbour and a knoll south of Reed's beach (hill noise); the 2.4 m bridge could bunch a crowd.

What changed in round 3

1. Harbour yard spaced: the seaplane moved out to (27.3, 21.4), fully afloat with only its nose at the sand line at (24.2, 23); the landing spot is at (20.5, 22.5), 3.7 m from the nose; the sign at (23, 29.2) is 6.3 m from the nose and 7 m from the landing spot; Reed stands 4 m off the nose. Crates went to the Fishmonger's yard at (22.8, 36.5) with the barrels at (16, 33.5).

2. Old Salty now walks x 0.8 between z 10.5 and z 1.2, turning round 1.2 m short of the bridge's landward end at z 0, so he never steps onto it. Spawn shifted to x −0.5 so he passes beside new players rather than through them.

3. A stop halfway up the road at the blue house's front: lit lamp (8, 41.5), bench (9.5, 42.8) facing the square, flower bed (6.5, 42.3). The road lamp at (2.7, 41) became an unlit glowing post, so point lights stay at 8.

4. Nothing else moved; the render shows no clashes and the terrain scan finds one connected water body.

The current map, for comparison

What the judges held against it. Everything used daily sits along one 60 m axis: a 23 m pier, then the stall and smokehouse 15 m behind its foot, the boards further on, the mirror behind a fence, the gate at the far end. The town is a mirrored template (houses at ±15 and ±9, paired lamps and flower beds). Reed's harbour, the Furthest Out board and the campfire are strung along the west rim and the campfire has no view. The shore is a plain bowl with no cove, point or silhouette.

Walks today: pier end to shop 6.3 s, shop to smokehouse 2.7 s, shop to gate 8.4 s, pier end to gate 14.5 s.

How they were judged

Four agents each designed a layout to the same brief (requirements, engine ground rules, performance budget, the game's style) and rendered it with one shared plan tool that mirrors the engine's shore, bank and dock rules, so sand, grass and water are where the game would put them and walks are measured, not guessed.

Each plan was scored 1-5 on eight points: the first ten seconds at spawn; hub legibility (shop, smokehouse, boards and mirror within a glance of the pier's foot); loop tightness (pier end, shop, smokehouse, back); cozy density (pockets with purpose, nothing on walking lines); lake framing; night (lamps leading pier to hub to gate, at most 8 point lights, as today); distinctiveness from today; and buildability.

  • Round 1: four concepts (harbour crescent, boardwalk and hillside, the point, a free take called the Quay). All four advanced with fixes. Common faults: a crammed harbour beach, quays drawn on sand, the square as a dead end up the hill.
  • Round 2: all four revised. The Quay dropped as the weaker twin of the boardwalk; its best ideas (a far silhouette for the fishing view, a lookout campfire, staggered houses) were passed to the finalists.
  • Round 3: polish only for the three finalists, plus each author's summary.

Budgets held by all three: 6 houses, 8 point lights, 4-5 dock rects, 60-70 small props (today about 50), no new textures or shaders, footprint within 46 x 64 m (today 37 x 61 m).
